title: Development of a non-contact and application-free camera system with short-wave infrared light for the detection of lymph nodes
summary:
The lymphatic system is an important pathway through which tumor cells can spread in the body.In tumor surgery, the TNM classification helps to assess tumor size, spread to neighboring lymph nodes and the formation of metastases (distant metastases). This assessment is crucial for the choice of treatment and for the patient's prognosis.

To determine the exact spread of the tumor, a minimum number of lymph nodes are determined that must be removed and examined during the operation.For example, 16 lymph nodes must be removed in the case of stomach cancer.The precise analysis of these lymph nodes is important in order to correctly assess the patient's prognosis.

Lymph nodes are often difficult to distinguish from fatty tissue, which is a challenge for surgeons and pathologists. During surgery, surgeons use their experience and existing guidelines to remove the correct lymph nodes. Afterwards, the lymph nodes are examined more closely in the laboratory.

Currently, infrared light is used to make lymph nodes more visible during the examination. The near infrared light helps to distinguish lymph nodes from fatty tissue because the lymph nodes contain more water and therefore absorb more light. The fatty tissue reflects more light and appears brighter.

A group of researchers at the University Hospital Dresden has developed a device that uses this principle to make lymph nodes more visible.

This device is to be used both in the laboratory and in the operating room to better identify and examine the lymph nodes during tumor surgery.In this way, the patient's treatment and prognosis can be made even more precise.
conditions: Patients undergoing bowel resection (patients with malignant and benign disease)
Patients undergoing resection in the head/neck area (patients with malignant and benign diseases)

interventions.name: Identification of lymph nodes in fatty tissue using an infrared camera

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients undergoing elective gastrointestinal surgery at the Clinic for Visceral, Thoracic, and Vascular Surgery or patients undergoing resection in the head/neck area at the Clinic for Ear, Nose, and Throat Medicine.
- Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients not capable of being informed
